# Story 1.1: Enrol an authenticator app
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder, I want to enrol an authenticator app by scanning a QR code, so that my account can be protected by a time-based one-time password.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a signed-in user without 2FA, when they start enrolment, then they see a QR code that an authenticator app can scan.
- AC-2: Given a user who has started enrolment, when they submit a valid code generated by their authenticator app, then 2FA is shown as enabled on their account.
- AC-3: Given a user who has started enrolment, when they submit an invalid code, then they see an error and 2FA remains not enabled.
- AC-4: Given a user who has started enrolment but not confirmed a code, when they next sign in, then no TOTP code is requested.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Generate a TOTP secret with pyotp, store it in the `totp_secret` column of the users table, and render its provisioning URI as a QR code (AC: 1)
- [ ] Add the confirmation step that verifies one submitted code with pyotp and only then marks 2FA as enabled (AC: 2, 3)
- [ ] Keep enrolment pending until confirmation so an unconfirmed secret never triggers a TOTP prompt at sign-in (AC: 4)

## Dev Notes
- FR-1 is the requirement behind this story. Architecture: the secret is stored in a new `totp_secret` column on the users table, and verification uses pyotp with no new service.

### References
- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-1]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#data-model]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#verification]

# Story 1.2: Sign in with a TOTP code
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder with 2FA enabled, I want sign-in to ask for a code from my authenticator app after my password, so that someone who knows only my password cannot get into my account.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a user with 2FA enabled, when they submit a correct password, then they are asked for a TOTP code and are not yet signed in.
- AC-2: Given a user at the TOTP step, when they submit a valid code, then they are signed in with a session cookie.
- AC-3: Given a user at the TOTP step, when they submit an invalid code, then they see an error and are not signed in.
- AC-4: Given a user without 2FA enabled, when they submit a correct password, then they are signed in without being asked for a code.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Split the session-cookie login into a password step and a TOTP step, issuing the signed-in session only after the second step when 2FA is enabled (AC: 1, 2, 4)
- [ ] Verify the submitted code against the user's `totp_secret` with pyotp and show an error on failure (AC: 2, 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-2 is the requirement behind this story. Architecture: the existing Flask app uses a session-cookie login, and TOTP verification uses pyotp with no new service.

### References
- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-2]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#verification]

# Story 1.3: Recover access with a recovery code
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder who has lost my authenticator device, I want to sign in with a single-use recovery code, so that I can regain access to my account.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a user who confirms enrolment, when enrolment completes, then they are shown ten recovery codes.
- AC-2: Given a user with 2FA enabled at the TOTP step, when they submit an unused recovery code instead of a TOTP code, then they are signed in.
- AC-3: Given a recovery code that has already been used to sign in, when it is submitted again, then sign-in is refused with an error.
- AC-4: Given a user who has used one recovery code, when they check their remaining codes, then nine remain usable.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Generate ten recovery codes at enrolment, store them in the `recovery_codes` column of the users table, and display them to the user once (AC: 1)
- [ ] Accept a recovery code in place of a TOTP code at the sign-in TOTP step (AC: 2)
- [ ] Mark a recovery code as consumed when used and reject it on any later attempt (AC: 3, 4)

## Dev Notes
- FR-3 is the requirement behind this story. Architecture: recovery codes are stored in a new `recovery_codes` column on the users table, with no new service.

### References
- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-3]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#data-model]
